early_look.title: Quad 2→3 Transition: Positioning for Inflation Acceleration
early_look.keith_thesis: Quad shift Q2→Q3 is emerging. Sold XLI, shorted XRT, sold IBIT, staying long QTUM. Long energy (XOP, OIH), telecom (XTL), and commodity inflation plays. Short housing (ITB), healthcare (XLV), retail (XRT), airlines (JETS).
keith_notes: Sold XLI — industrials move to headwind in Quad 3
Shorted XRT — consumer discretionary/retail short in Quad 3
Sold IBIT — Bitcoin a headwind in Quad 3
Staying long QTUM — secular quantum theme holds across quad shift
Quad 3 longs: XOP, OIH, XTL, EQRR, QTUM, ROBO

With industry consolidation accelerating and a structurally advantaged sourcing model, MUSA offers a differentiated and durable way to play both energy and consumer trends.

RBLX.thesis: Roblox (RBLX) remains a short with slowing user growth. Freedman's data is pointing to much lower daily active user (DAU) and bookings growth than investors saw last quarter. After a sharp bounce in the stock, expectations remain too high relative to the clear deceleration in engagement trends and post-holiday activity. With growth normalizing and management guiding to slower momentum ahead, the risk is that estimates come down and the stock re-rates lower.
RBLX.weekend_update: RBLX remains a Short as decelerating new user growth, reduced bookings guidance, and multiple near-term headwinds converge into a high-risk Q3 trough setup...

ONON.thesis: ONON is a short as the CEO departure signals an inflection toward slower growth, while current profitability and expectations remain unsustainably high. With gross margins above 60% and heavily concentrated product exposure, the company faces meaningful downside as scale drives margin normalization and competitive pressures from Nike intensify. In a Quad 3 backdrop with bearish signal strength, decelerating growth and overly optimistic sell-side assumptions set up for estimate cuts and multiple compression.
ONON.weekend_update: ONON remains a Short as slowing growth across key segments, weakening direct-to-consumer trends, and ongoing management uncertainty continue to challenge the durability of the premium growth and margin narrative...

Slowing comps, declining store productivity, and overexpansion into lower-quality locations point to an inevitable trade-off between unit growth and margins. With the business likely transitioning to ex-growth and valuation still in “no man’s land,” the stock faces meaningful downside as multiple compression accelerates.
OLLI.weekend_update: OLLI remains a high-conviction short as deteriorating traffic trends, weakening new-store productivity, and overly optimistic comp expectations continue to pressure the underlying growth narrative...
